standard.coverage: Employers with FOUR OR MORE employees, excluding family members (820 ILCS 105/3(d)).
standard.note: Final step of SB 1 (2019). No escalator -- Illinois is flat at $15.00 until the legislature acts.

tipped.note: 820 ILCS 105/4(c) caps the tip credit at 40% of the minimum wage, so the cash wage is 60% -- $9.00. Chicago is separately phasing its tip credit out entirely; see local/IL-local-2026.json.

variants.label: Employees under 18 working fewer than 650 hours in a calendar year
variants.test: Under 18 AND fewer than 650 hours worked for the employer in the calendar year. Crossing 650 hours moves the employee to the full $15.00 for the rest of the year.
variants.note: 820 ILCS 105/4(a)(2). A genuine hours-tracking obligation, not just an age test.

youthAndTraining.label: New employee, first 90 consecutive calendar days (18 or older)
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employee 18 or older during the first 90 consecutive calendar days after initial employment by the employer; not available for day or temporary laborers. An option for the employer, not a requirement. 820 ILCS 105/4(a)(2).
youthAndTraining.source: Illinois Minimum Wage Law 820 ILCS 105/4 https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/ilcs/fulltext.asp?DocName=082001050K4 read directly 2026-11-07: (a)(2) an employer may pay an employee 18 or older, during the first 90 consecutive calendar days after initial employment, a wage not more than 50 cents less than the (a)(1) wage, except that a day or temporary laborer (the excerpt read ends the exception list after item (A)) must be paid the full wage; (a)(3) an employee under 18 who has not worked more than 650 hours for the employer in the calendar year is paid 13 dollars an hour on and after January 1, 2025, and more than 650 hours the (a)(1) adult wage.

youthAndTraining.label: Under 18, up to 650 hours in the calendar year
youthAndTraining.eligibility: Employee under 18 who has not worked more than 650 hours for the employer in the calendar year; after 650 hours the adult wage applies. 820 ILCS 105/4(a)(3).
youthAndTraining.source: Illinois Minimum Wage Law 820 ILCS 105/4 https://www.ilga.gov/legislation/ilcs/fulltext.asp?DocName=082001050K4 read directly 2026-11-07: (a)(2) an employer may pay an employee 18 or older, during the first 90 consecutive calendar days after initial employment, a wage not more than 50 cents less than the (a)(1) wage, except that a day or temporary laborer (the excerpt read ends the exception list after item (A)) must be paid the full wage; (a)(3) an employee under 18 who has not worked more than 650 hours for the employer in the calendar year is paid 13 dollars an hour on and after January 1, 2025, and more than 650 hours the (a)(1) adult wage.

knownGaps: Chicago and suburban Cook County set higher local rates on a July 1 cycle -- see local/IL-local-2026.json.
